narratives.Overview:
# feat(review-cycle,swarm): policy-anchored review-response loop — classify reviewer findings against a written invariant before patching; batch fixes into one push

Parent umbrella: #2018 (Review lane)

## Summary

When automated review (Greptile/SLizard) comments on a swarm PR, the responding agent today patches finding-by-finding and pushes per patch. Each push triggers a fresh review round against brand-new code, and for invariant-shaped findings (concurrency, error policy, containment) each patch opens the next window. Mechanism: before any code change in response to a reviewer finding, the agent must anchor the affected code to a **written policy** (invariant / error-policy / threat-model header comment or design note, adding one if absent), classify each finding as in-model (patch) or out-of-model (accepted-risk reply citing the anchor), consolidate all in-scope fixes into **one** commit, run the local review pass, and push once. A loop signal (rounds > 3 on the same file, or #3448's same-fingerprint detector) escalates to a design pass (#3434 motion) instead of running round K+1.

Internalize as a skill (working name `deft-directive-review-response`) so the motion is framework-scaffolded instead of operator-driven.

## The gap

Two same-day exemplar arcs (2026-08-17/18), both operator-noticed; the framework never prompted either:

- **PR #3440** (occupancy lease, #3433): six Greptile/SLizard rounds on `occupancy.ts`/`lock.ts`. Every fix to the hand-rolled file lock introduced the next TOCTOU (non-atomic claim → lock file → abandoned-lock deadlock → blind timeout unlink → PID-reclaim unlink race), plus one self-authorization defect introduced *by* a fix (closeout adopting the lease identity it read off disk). The findings were individually legitimate; the loop was structural. Resolution required an ownership-fence redesign plus a stated concurrency model — a motion no per-finding patch converges to.
- **PR #3436** (intended-placement preflight, #3424): six rounds on one file, oscillating between throw-on-error and skip-on-error — each swing generating the opposite finding — then escalating into adversarial-local-TOCTOU territory that a stated threat model would have scoped out in round one. Meanwhile the two findings that actually block shipping (fail-closed bricks pre-existing vBRIEFs; issue-ingest births briefs that cannot preflight) arrived only in the final round, after the loop had consumed the budget.

Same shape as #3434's finding on triage and #1140's original capture: the value-producing work was operator-noticed and operator-driven; the framework never prompted it. The conventions exist (#1152 current-shape, accepted-risk replies) — the framework just doesn't prompt the composition.

### Adjacent prior art (distinct, composes)

- **#1225** (operator-driven quality ratchet) proposes the review-cycle iteration model and a finding-triage taxonomy (`fix` / `false-positive-dismiss` / `defer-with-issue`), but supplies no *basis* for the classification — nothing tells the agent what makes a finding a false positive rather than a fix. This issue supplies that basis (the policy anchor).
- **#3448** (standing residual until conf floor or same-fingerprint loop) governs **when to stop pushing** — park vs continue. This issue governs **how to respond while continuing**. The two exemplars above failed by over-eager patching; #3448's field class failed by premature parking. Complementary halves; this issue reuses #3448's loop detector rather than inventing a parallel one.

## Mechanism

1. **Policy anchor precondition.** A review-response pass on invariant-shaped findings (concurrency, error handling, containment/security) may not edit code until the affected module carries a written policy: assumptions, guarantees, non-goals. Absent → writing it is the first work item. This supplies the classification basis #1225's Gap-1 triage taxonomy currently lacks: in-model → fix; out-of-model → accepted-risk reply citing the anchor; anchor-wrong → revise the anchor first, then fix.
2. **Batch discipline.** One consolidated commit per review round; local review pass before push; never push per finding. Each per-finding push triggers a fresh reviewer round against brand-new code and restarts the loop.
3. **Escalation on loop detection.** Compose with #3448's same-fingerprint loop detector and add a rounds tripwire (> 3 review rounds touching the same file): where #3448 resolves park-vs-continue, this issue resolves *how* to continue — the exit from a detected loop on invariant-shaped findings is a design pass (#3434 motion), not round K+1 and not parking. Both exemplar battles ran 6 rounds; the tripwire fires at round 3–4 in each, before the worst defects (a fix that introduced self-authorization on #3440; adversarial-TOCTOU escalation on #3436) occurred.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-18T03:36:47Z)

## Field note — header anchors are load-bearing for this mechanism

When the 3382 orchestrator finishes the consolidated redesigns on **PR #3440** (#3433 occupancy) and **PR #3436** (#3424 intended-placement), it MUST verify the pushed commits actually include the **policy / threat-model header comments**, not only the code fixes.

Those anchors are what accepted-risk replies cite. They are also what this issue's mechanism depends on: classify each finding as in-model (patch) vs out-of-model (accepted-risk reply citing the header). If a later pass drops the headers as "just comments," the next review round has nothing to classify against, and the loop this issue is supposed to stop starts again.

Concrete check on the pushed HEAD (not the worktree mid-edit):

- `#3440` / `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` — concurrency model: assumptions (local FS, cooperating processes), guarantees (mutex / detect-and-abort), non-goals (network FS, Byzantine, perfect off-Linux PID reuse).
- `#3436` / `packages/core/src/preflight/intended-placement.ts` — error policy (fail closed except first-touch ENOENT) + threat model (preflight is a quality gate on the agent's own plan; adversarial-local TOCTOU is a non-goal beyond fd discipline).

If either header is missing on the pushed SHA, that is a product hole in the redesign batch, not a style nit. Do not start accepted-risk replies until the anchor is on HEAD.

Mid-flight (2026-08-18, worktrees not yet the merge SHA): both headers are present in the local redesign trees. Re-verify after the one-push lands.

This is also an AC seed for this issue: the skill / review-response pass must refuse to classify out-of-model findings until a written anchor exists on the current HEAD of the file under review.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-18T04:10:54Z)

## Operational cite for tonight — slizard#2694

https://github.com/deftai/slizard/issues/2694

SLizard's arity checker compares **head call sites** against the **base-revision** definition. When a PR widens a signature and updates its call sites together, it posts a 93%-confidence P1 that is false on the head blob.

Until slizard fixes that: any 93%-confidence arity P1 on a PR that touches the named function's signature is **presumed false**. Check the head blob first. A one-line falsification reply with this issue link is enough — do not re-derive the full evidence each time.

Field use: PR 3453 `printUpdateComplete` (4 params at `refresh.ts:732`, calls at 1225/1227). Same class as the 3432 `formatRefusal` false P1.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-18T13:45:16Z)

## Sequence-end field evidence — PR 3453 arc (2026-08-18)

#3452 stays **open**. This is the tripwire exemplar, not a close.

PR **#3453** / #3437 is the richest field run of this issue's mechanism: classify against a written invariant, one batch, escalate on loop instead of round K+1.

### Arc

| Step | HEAD | Score | Outcome |
|------|------|-------|---------|
| Derive-the-plan + parity test | `5e4816e2` | 2/5 | **(d)** — collect-only still hit raw `rmSync` / stale dest postcondition. Escalated; scoped precursor **#3456** / PR **#3458** (merged `82bd37f3`). |
| Rebase onto #3458 | `6ab09c2c` | 2/5 | **(d)** again — `removeStaleMigratedFrameworkNarrative` still raw-deleted under collect-only; name-only `replaceTree` listed writes without opening contents. |
| Operator-ruled final batch (static enforcement + fixture completion) | red `da794d82` → green `2f6e4ce1` | **3/5** SHA-match | Prior two P1s closed (stale-narrative routed through `containedRemove`; collect-only `replaceTree` now opens and compares). New confirmed in-model residuals: (1) **plan fidelity** — atomic slash/OpenClaw dests omitted under collect-only; (2) **dest mutation** — `writeConsumerGitHooks` still runs `git config core.hooksPath` on dry-run. |

Independent `pr:watch --one-shot` on `2f6e4ce1`: `sha_match=true`, `confidence=3`, `p0=0`, `p1=0`, `clean_gate_holdout=has_blocking`, merge-gate green. **(b′)** — not floored, not merged.

### What the tripwire did

The pre-committed stop fired: one more confirmed in-model P1 in the chokepoint / plan-fidelity class **halts**. No fourth product batch. Escalation comment: https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3453#issuecomment-5329051010

Named alternative now on the table (**#3434-style critique**, not another instance chase):

**materialize-and-diff** — dry-run projects content into a scratch directory outside the project root using the **same write code** (no collect-only mode) and diffs the result against the live tree. That eliminates the mode-divergence class at the cost of temp I/O. Collect-only did not stabilize after precursor + static enforcement.

### Adjacent field from the same night (headers / classification basis)

- PR **#3440** / #3433 occupancy — concurrency-model header survived merge (`084371c0`). 5/5 (a).
- PR **#3436** / #3424 placement — error-policy + threat-model headers. Recovered 5/5 (a) after disposition-before-score.
- slizard#2694 arity false-positive class (this comment thread, 2026-08-18) remains the cite for 93% arity P1s on widened signatures.

#3437 stays open with 3453. Park-exit taxonomy remains **#3457** (not this issue).

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-18T15:46:43Z)

## #3462 outcome (operator accepted 2026-08-18)

Accepted: **side-effect port (construction-level collection)**. 3453 disposition **replace**.

ADR is `docs/decisions/ADR-004-update-dry-run-plan.md` (landing with the salvage PR). Three acceptance conditions are in the ADR: (1) enforcement legs — static ban extended to dest-mutating `child_process`/`git` plus the zero-mutation fixture; (2) migration is consolidation of the 3 existing dest-mutating seams (`GitHooksSeams`, `copyContent`, `runOrgForceOn`), not a fresh wrapper; (3) honest exclusions label survives and shrinks, never silently disappears.

Acceptance: https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3462#issuecomment-5330417455


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-18T16:20:03Z)

## Field validation + AC deltas (2026-08-18, pass-type: field-evidence — pickup-ready)

The mechanism was executed manually end-to-end across PRs #3432 / #3436 / #3440 / #3451 / #3453 / #3464 tonight. It works; implement as specced with the deltas below.

**Anchors did the work.** Policy headers written before responding (occupancy.ts concurrency model on #3440; error-policy + threat-model on #3436; plan-completeness contract on #3453) made classification mechanical in both directions: out-of-model findings got anchor-citing replies (fence guarantee, one-cohort-per-worktree, ancestor-symlink), in-model findings got batched fixes. Pre-anchor, #3440 and #3436 each burned 6 whack-a-mole rounds; post-anchor, rounds resolved in minutes.

**Calibration datum for the classify step (new AC):** six deterministic SLizard P1s across three PRs; five false, one real. Root cause of the five: the checker reads definitions from the merge-base blob while call sites come from head (deftai/slizard#2694). AC addition: classification of any deterministic arity/wiring claim MUST include a head-blob check (`git show <head-sha>:<file>`) before it can be confirmed; when the PR itself changes the named symbol, presume false and verify. The one real hit (dead export on #3440) proves blanket dismissal is wrong — check every time.

**Tripwire validated, including the exit:** #3453 hit (d) twice under a pre-committed stop; the exits executed as designed — first a scoped precursor (#3458), then a design pass (#3462 → side-effect-port ADR) instead of round K+1. Full arc in the comment above.

**Composition (do not duplicate):** #3448/PR #3451 (shipped) governs park-vs-continue; #3457 governs how parks exit (floor-distance, stable-floor); #3434 is where (d) escalations go. This issue owns only: anchor precondition, classify-then-act (incl. head-blob check), batch discipline (one consolidated push per review round; riders allowed on mechanical rebases), and the rounds tripwire (>3 on one file).
